column2: Carlo Nallino, who has taken care of establishing and correcting the text of this book, says: All the chapters are complete, and in the Escorial copy the tables follow them. We, however, have taken from them only what concerns chronology, geography and the names of the fixed stars, and have printed it without correcting the errors and the corruptions in the abjad letters — and, by God, how many these mistakes are! Whoever wishes to correct them should consult our Latin translation of this book, in which we have also printed the rest of the tables, which contain numbers only.

The reader must also be told that the abjad letters have the same values in the tables as in the Escorial copy, that is, by the usage of the people of the West: so Ṣ stands for 60, Ḍ for 90, S for 300 and Ẓ for 800.
